questions.q: Why does a country need a constitution, and how was the Indian Constitution made?

answer.text: A constitution is the supreme law that expresses a society's shared ideals, defines how the government is to be formed and what powers it has, sets limits on those powers, and guarantees the rights of citizens. It builds trust and coordination among diverse people, as the example of post-apartheid South Africa shows.

It was framed by the Constituent Assembly, which worked from 1946 to 1949 and had 299 members. Dr Rajendra Prasad was its President and Dr B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee. The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950. It drew on the ideals of the freedom struggle and on the experience of other democracies.

questions.q: What are the values enshrined in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
answer: The Preamble is the introduction to the Constitution and sets out the values on which the Republic is founded.

answer.text: It begins with the words 'We, the People of India', declaring that the Constitution draws its authority from the people themselves.

It describes India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic — sovereign meaning free to decide its own affairs, socialist meaning aiming at social and economic equality, secular meaning equal respect for all religions, democratic meaning ruled by elected representatives, and a republic meaning the head of state is elected.
It promises to secure for all citizens justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, so that every individual enjoys dignity and unity is maintained.
